note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Bregman proximal viewpoint: layer definition, unification, Bregman variant, expressivity and experiments

nodes.name: Operator learning goal
nodes.description: Operator learning seeks the unknown ground-truth operator G between separable Banach function spaces A and U from N input-output function pairs, e.g. mapping a PDE initial condition to its solution at a later time.

nodes.name: Classical neural operator form
nodes.description: A neural operator is a composition of a lifting operator P, T operator layers L_t (each involving a linear operator K_t, bias b_t and a pointwise activation), and a projection operator Q.

nodes.name: Layers as Bregman-regularized minimizers
nodes.description: Each operator layer can be defined as the minimizer of a Bregman-regularized optimization problem over function spaces, so the activation operator is implicitly defined as a Bregman proximity operator.

nodes.name: Unification of classical operators
nodes.description: When the Bregman distance is Euclidean and Psi_t is built from a strongly convex Legendre function psi, the layer reduces to the gradient of the conjugate, nabla Psi*_t(M_t v + K_t v + b_t), recovering a broad class of classical neural operator layers (Proposition 3.4).

nodes.name: Bregman neural operators
nodes.description: For a general p-uniformly convex Legendre psi (not the squared norm) and g_t=0, the layer takes a Bregman form that includes the inverse activation operator, defining a new family of Bregman neural operators (Proposition 3.5).

nodes.name: Bregman FNO (BFNO)
nodes.description: Specializing to Fourier layers with convolutional kernels on the torus gives the Bregman Fourier neural operator, whose update has the form v_{t+1}=sigma(sigma^{-1}(v_t)+K_t v_t) with the linear operator outside the activation.

nodes.name: Universal approximation
nodes.description: For sigmoidal-type homeomorphic activations, Bregman neural operators are universal approximators of continuous operators on compact sets: for any epsilon there is N_theta with sup error at most epsilon (Theorem 4.1).

nodes.name: BFNO depth scaling
nodes.description: On 2D Navier-Stokes (nu=1e-4), BFNO achieves lower error for every depth T; FNO degrades from T=8 and ResFNO from T=16, while F-FNO improves until T=16 and BFNO until T=64.

nodes.name: BFNO competitive across datasets
nodes.description: With cross-validated depth T in {4,8,16,32}, BFNO is consistently superior or comparable to FNO, ResFNO and F-FNO, with notable gains on 1D Burgers and 2D Navier-Stokes (nu=1e-4); 2D Darcy is the exception.

nodes.name: ODE view explains stability
nodes.description: Under z_t=sigma^{-1}(v_t), BFNO is a discretization of dz/dt=K(t)sigma(z), whereas residual architectures discretize dv/dt=sigma(K(t)v); placing the linear operator outside the activation mitigates vanishing gradients differently.

nodes.name: BFNO weights cluster at zero
nodes.description: BFNO's learned weights are sharply peaked at 0 (Laplace-like) while FNO, ResFNO and F-FNO are Gaussian-like, suggesting implicit regularization toward identity and mitigation of vanishing/exploding gradients.

isolated_nodes.name: Darcy exception
isolated_nodes.description: On 2D Darcy, which maps a viscosity function to a steady-state solution, F-FNO outperforms BFNO, plausibly due to its extra MLP layers capturing the viscosity-to-solution dependencies.

isolated_nodes.name: Frequency-band results
isolated_nodes.description: BFNO consistently outperforms FNO in low and mid frequency bands; in the high band, gains are substantial on simple datasets but marginal on complex ones.

isolated_nodes.name: Theory-practice gap
isolated_nodes.description: The universal approximation result covers sigmoidal activations, whereas common practice relies on ReLU-like activations, leaving a theoretical gap.

structural_reasoning: The paper builds from the layer-as-optimization definition to unification and a new Bregman variant, which supports expressivity and experimental claims. Frequency-band, Darcy and gap remarks are isolated.
